CHIEF COMPLAINT
Yearly exam

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Beverly is a 24-year-old female presenting for her annual examination. She reports that she has been doing well overall. She began working in a bakery this summer and finds the work enjoyable. However, she notes that due to her proximity to many desserts at work, she has been snacking frequently and consuming significantly more desserts than usual. She acknowledges that her diet has been poor lately as a result of work-related temptation, which she finds challenging to resist. She reports that her blood sugars have been up and down, which she attributes to her dietary changes. However, she confirms that she has been taking her diabetes medication as prescribed without missing doses. Regarding her hypertension, she reports that her blood pressure has been good despite the fluctuations in her diabetes levels. She denies any safety concerns.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
No additional concerns reported. Patient reports sleeping well with a full eight hours nightly. Denies suicidal or self-harm ideation.

Type 2 diabetes mellitus

Grade 2 systolic ejection murmur (unchanged from prior exams)

Not documented

Patient works in a bakery, which she began this summer and finds enjoyable. She acknowledges difficulty resisting desserts and treats in the workplace.

Pulmonary: Lungs clear bilaterally

RESULTS
Hemoglobin A1C: Elevated

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Diabetes mellitus type 2: Currently out of control with elevated hemoglobin A1C. Goal is to achieve A1C less than 7, preferably under 6. Assessment is that poor glycemic control is diet-related. Continue metformin twice daily without change at this time. Patient instructed to reduce snacking and limit additional sweets. Patient to check blood glucose in the morning and call in fasting blood sugar results in approximately 2 weeks. Follow-up appointment in approximately 2 months. If glycemic control does not improve with dietary modifications, will consider adding additional antidiabetic medication.

2. Hypertension: Relatively stable and well-controlled on current regimen. Continue lisinopril 10 mg once daily. No medication changes at this time.
